subject: Cloud Computing
title: Governance at Scale
description: A quick win: understand Governance at Scale.

hook.text: A large company has 500 cloud accounts, 10,000 resources, and 2,000 users. Who ensures the rules are followed?

buildup.text: Cloud governance means policies, guardrails, and automation that enforce security across all accounts.

discovery.text: Tools like AWS Organizations, Azure Policy, and GCP Organization Policies set rules that apply everywhere.

twist.text: Governance too strict kills innovation. Governance too loose creates security chaos. The balance is delicate.

climax.text: The best cloud governance is invisible: developers move fast while guardrails quietly prevent disasters.

punchline.text: Good governance is invisible. You only notice it when it's missing.

quiz.question: What is the goal of cloud governance?
options: Enforcing security policies across all accounts while still enabling innovation
Giving every user unrestricted access to all cloud resources
Eliminating the need for any human oversight in the cloud

details.summary: Cloud governance establishes organizational policies, guardrails, and account structures that enforce security and compliance at scale. Landing zones, service control policies, and organizational units ensure that every new account inherits baseline security automatically.
details.whyItMatters: Without governance, cloud environments sprawl into ungovernable configurations. Centralized guardrails prevent misconfiguration before it happens, at scale.
takeaways: Landing zones establish secure baseline configurations
Service control policies enforce guardrails across all accounts
Organizational units group accounts by function or compliance

faq.question: What is a cloud landing zone?
faq.answer: A landing zone is a pre-configured, secure multi-account environment with networking, IAM, logging, and security guardrails already in place. New workloads deploy into this governed structure rather than starting from blank accounts, ensuring consistent security from day one.

faq.question: How do service control policies work?
faq.answer: SCPs set permission boundaries at the organization or account level that cannot be overridden by individual IAM policies. They prevent actions like disabling logging, creating resources in unapproved regions, or disabling encryption, regardless of user permissions.
